# Vasectomy Reversal — Authorization Guide

_Subtitle: CPT Codes · ICD-10 · Payer Requirements_

_backHref: /vasectomy-reversal_

## CPT Codes

| CPT | Description | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 55400 | Vasovasostomy, vasovasorrhaphy | Primary |
| 54900 | Epididymovasostomy, unilateral | Primary |
| 54901 | Epididymovasostomy, bilateral | Primary |
| 55250 | Vasectomy, unilateral or bilateral (separate procedure), including postoperative semen examination(s) | Related |
| 76872 | Ultrasound, transrectal | Diagnostic |
| 89300 | Semen analysis; presence and/or motility of sperm including Huhner test (post coital) | Diagnostic |

## ICD-10 Diagnoses

| ICD-10 | Description |
| --- | --- |
| N46.01 | Organic azoospermia |
| N46.021 | Azoospermia due to obstructive causes |
| N46.029 | Azoospermia due to other obstructive causes |
| N46.11 | Organic oligospermia |
| Z30.2 | Encounter for sterilization (vasectomy status) |
| Z31.0 | Encounter for reversal of previous sterilization |
| N50.89 | Other specified disorders of male genital organs |

## Coverage Landscape

### Common Denial Reasons

- "Elective/voluntary sterilization reversal" exclusion
- "Infertility treatment" blanket exclusion
- "Not medically necessary" (fertility not a covered benefit)

### Strongest Coverage Arguments

- State mandate for infertility coverage (15+ states require coverage)
- Obstructive azoospermia as a diagnosable medical condition (N46.021)
- Reversal is more cost-effective than IVF/ICSI over multiple cycles
- AUA/ASRM guidelines support reversal as first-line treatment for obstructive azoospermia

## Prior Authorization Requirements

### Required Documentation

- Semen analysis (azoospermia or severe oligospermia)
- Vasectomy operative report or confirmation of vasectomy status
- Years since vasectomy (obstructive interval)
- Female partner age and fertility evaluation results
- FSH, LH, testosterone levels
- Scrotal ultrasound if epididymal obstruction suspected
- Letter of medical necessity from urologist/reproductive specialist

### Medical Necessity Criteria

- Documented azoospermia on ≥2 semen analyses
- Obstructive etiology confirmed (normal FSH, normal testicular volume)
- Desire for biological paternity with current partner
- Female partner fertility evaluation completed (or documented attempt)
- Microsurgical expertise available (fellowship-trained microsurgeon)

### Cost-Effectiveness Argument

Vasectomy reversal ($5,000–$15,000 one-time) is significantly more cost-effective than IVF/ICSI ($12,000–$20,000 per cycle) when the female partner is <37 years and obstructive interval is <15 years. ASRM Practice Committee guidelines explicitly recommend reversal as first-line treatment in appropriate candidates.
